_case_notes.dialogue_heavy: Capped at 0.80 by one invented name (a sous chef who is not in the transcript), and the CTA is incomplete. This is what a mediocre-but-shippable output scores.
_case_notes.ensemble_arc: Drops the two minor characters (Halden, Vesper) from an ensemble episode; everything else is clean.
_case_notes.near_empty: Floored by the hallucination cap: the fixture invents an entire cast for a transcript that contains nothing. 0.25 is the intended baseline, not a bug. An honest 'no usable transcript' output would score around 0.48, so a prompt fix that teaches the model to refuse here shows up as a large positive delta.
_case_notes.odd_formatting: Loses 0.10 to an introduction the prompt explicitly forbids. The model obeys the CTA instruction and disobeys the no-intro one, which is exactly the sort of asymmetry this rubric exists to surface.
_case_notes.short_episode: Clean baseline. Anything below ~0.95 here is a real regression.

_comment: Committed baseline. This file is the regression signal: a prompt change that makes
generation worse shows up here as a diff in a code review, which is the whole point.
Regenerate with:  python evals/run_eval.py --mode live --record   (re-records fixtures)
Never update the baseline in the same commit as a prompt change without saying in the
commit message which numbers moved and why.
The gate: CI fails if the aggregate drops below min_aggregate_score, if any single case
regresses by more than max_case_regression, or if the shipped prompt stops issuing an
instruction the rubric scores (the prompt-contract check).
min_aggregate_score is set ~0.02 under the current aggregate: tight enough to catch a
real regression, loose enough that rounding noise does not fail a build.
